content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 6-7 and 16. Supplemental: C4 system context guidance. This unit focuses on architectural scope and responsibility.

Architecture scope determines which concerns the architecture must address. Scope can be product-level, system-level, subsystem-level, platform-level, or enterprise-level. Confusion about scope causes teams to over-design local details or under-design cross-cutting decisions.

Responsibility boundaries clarify ownership. A module, service, component, team, or external provider may own a decision. The architecture should make ownership clear enough that future changes have accountable paths.
Studio: classify five decisions from a current app as product, system, subsystem, or component-scope decisions.

concepts.name: Architecture scope
concepts.description: The span of system, organization, lifecycle, and decision-making concerns covered by an architecture effort.

concepts.name: Responsibility boundary
concepts.description: A boundary that clarifies which element, team, or party owns a capability or decision.

concepts.name: Ownership model
concepts.description: The assignment of responsibility for architectural elements, decisions, operations, and change.

concepts.name: Scope creep
concepts.description: Expansion of expected responsibility beyond the agreed system boundary or architecture goal.
